children: Photography By Delali Ayivi for WSJ. Magazine | Text and Styling by Rashad Minnick

Working on this issue's feature on the Southern University Marching Band in Baton Rouge, La., was a full-circle moment for me: I returned to my alma mater, where I played the clarinet in the band from 2008 to 2014, through graduate school.

The marching band goes far beyond playing music; it instills life skills, creativity and discipline. Above all, it teaches the value of time. It starts with the pulse of the metronome keeping tempo and extends to showing up early for rehearsal. My band director, Lawrence Jackson, would remind us, "Early is on time; on time, you're late!"

For our shoot, photographer Delali Ayivi captured the students' tireless efforts to make halftime-show magic. When bad weather struck, she asked if students might be available the next day-a Saturday. "Absolutely; we have practice tomorrow!" assured the band's current director, Kedric Taylor. Rain or shine, they're out on the hot asphalt, playing their instruments.
Here, Southern University's Human Jukebox Marching Band, one of the country's top marching bands, shows off sport watches in the school's colors.
